'''Savoiardi''' are a sponge-like [[Cookbook:Cookie|cookie]] originally from the Aosta Valley of Italy in the Alps, once known as the Duchy of Savoy (whence its name is derived). They figure prominently in several [[Cookbook:Dessert|desserts]], including puddings and [[Cookbook:Tiramisù |tiramisu]], as they absorb liquids excellently.

== Ingredients ==
* 400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Flour|self raising flour]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Powder|baking powder]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white sugar]]
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Oil|oil]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* the [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|juice]] of 2 [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]]
* [[Cookbook:Powdered Sugar|Powdered sugar]]
* Pure [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla extract]]

== Procedure ==
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the eggs until very thick. Add sugar, oil, vanilla, baking powder, and lemon juice, and stir until combined.
# Slowly [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] in flour with a wooden spoon, continually adding until you have a very thick batter (you may need more or less flour).
# On a large flat surface, such as a cutting board or plate, [[Cookbook:Sifting|sift]] the powdered sugar.
# Using a teaspoon, scoop walnut-sized balls of batter onto the powdered sugar, and roll each into an oval.
# Transfer cookies to a [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|cookie sheet]] lined with [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment paper]], and cover with a single layer of parchment.
# Place pans into an [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] preheated to 200°C (392°F).
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] for 5–15 minutes, until biscotti begin to turn golden.
# Cool completely.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* If you choose to buy savoiardi in a store rather than make them, be sure of the date they were made as they have a very short shelf life.
* Properly made savoiardi should never be soft.
* Savoiardi are often enjoyed dipped in brandy and espresso coffee.

== Warnings ==
* Savoiardi absorb liquid very quickly. If too much liquid is absorbed then the cookie breaks and falls apart.

== External links ==
* [http://www.recipesource.com/desserts/cookies/08/rec0831.html Another recipe on RecipeSource]
* [http://italianfood.about.com/od/biscottietc/r/blr0702.htm Non-traditional recipe from About.com]
